name: moving vehicle floodwater simulation open source implementations
goal: I am building a numerical simulation of a passenger vehicle MOVING through a flooded roadway, in order to produce something the field appears to lack: a graded "safe crossing speed" surface as a joint function of water depth, floodwater flow velocity, and the vehicle's own travel speed. The existing vehicle-stability literature is almost entirely threshold-based and is derived from a STATIONARY vehicle exposed to flow. I need to know what has actually been done when the vehicle itself moves. I especially want papers that describe how the hydrodynamic force on the moving body is extracted and validated, and whether they operate in the body-fixed (moving reference frame) or ground-fixed frame. I also want anything on moving-reference-frame formulations for particle methods such as the material point method, and on refinement windows that follow a moving body through a large domain. My understanding is that this may be genuinely unaddressed, and I want to know whether that is true.
summary:
The literature contains only a small, distinct moving-vehicle evidence base: Shah's 1:10 Perodua Viva experiments varied vehicle motion and flow Froude number, reporting speed-dependent drag, buoyancy, friction and an incipient-velocity criterion [Sha18c, Sha19d, Sha20, Sha21], while Al-Qadami et al. added full-scale coupled CFD of a passenger car crossing incoming flow [Alq21, Alq22]. These studies still reduce stability to failure thresholds, not a continuous safe-speed surface resolving vehicle speed independently from current velocity; other vehicle-wading CFD generally prescribes speed and emphasizes water ingress or resistance [Ols18b, Xin21b, Var21].

REUSABLE IMPLEMENTATIONS.
- Open-source SPH/MBD coupling is the strongest directly reusable route: DualSPHysics [Cre15] with Project Chrono/DVI coupling [Can18, Maz18] and Chrono::FSI vehicle-fording models [Paz14, Paz16, Was15].
- OpenFOAM-based moving-body options include dynamic/overset meshes [Jas10, She15], FloatStepper with released code and added-mass treatment [Roe23], and signed-distance immersed boundaries (sdfibm) [Zha20o]. IBAMR provides open-source immersed-boundary/Brinkman multiphase implementations with force constraints rather than surface-stress integration [Bha19]; AMR moving-body IB is explicitly demonstrated in [Nan19].
- BODY-FIXED FORMULATIONS ARE ESTABLISHED FOR EULERIAN IB/LEVEL-SET SOLVERS [Yan09, Yan10] BUT ARE NOT EVIDENT AS A DEVELOPED MOVING-REFERENCE FORMULATION FOR MPM. MPM free-surface, rigid-coupling, and AMR components exist [Zha17c, Li22b, Hu18, Mao16], BUT A BODY-FOLLOWING REFINEMENT WINDOW APPEARS UNREPORTED.

VALIDATION ASSETS. Public or reproducible targets include full-scale/model vehicle tests [Alq21, Sha20], dam-break cylinder data with pressure/video supplements [Kam19], and a high-precision public floating-sphere decay dataset [Kra21b].
